uk: Big Ben is not the tower and not the clock - it is the nickname of the giant bell inside. The tower itself is called Elizabeth Tower, so most of us have been saying it wrong for years.
pt: Portugal and England signed their alliance in 1386 and it is still in force, making it the oldest alliance in the world. That is 600+ years of friendship without a single unfriending.
fr: On hot summer days the Eiffel Tower grows taller by up to about 15 centimeters, because the iron expands in the heat. It is basically stretching after a nap.
it: Rome has a whole other country inside it: Vatican City, the smallest country in the world. It is surprisingly easy to cross a border while looking for gelato.
de: Neuschwanstein Castle looks so much like a fairy tale that it is said to have inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle. Its king, Ludwig II, died before it was finished.
es: Work on the Sagrada Familia in Barcelona began in 1882 and the church is still not completely finished. It must be one of the longest-running building sites in history.
tas: Tasmanian devils are the largest meat-eating marsupials alive, and their screeches were so scary that early settlers named them after the devil. In real life they are only about the size of a small dog.
wa: Western Australia is more than three times the size of Texas and covers about a third of the whole of Australia. That leaves plenty of room for everyone to have a private desert.
sa: In Coober Pedy in South Australia, many people live underground in dugout homes to escape the scorching heat. There, a basement is not a luxury - it is the whole house.
vic: The Great Ocean Road in Victoria was built by soldiers returning from World War I, and it is a memorial to those who did not come home. It is often called the largest war memorial in the world, and it is also a very scenic commute.
qld: The Great Barrier Reef off Queensland is the largest coral reef system on Earth, bigger than Italy and big enough to be seen from space. Not bad for a neighborhood of tiny animals.
nz: In 1893 New Zealand became the first self-governing country to let women vote. The sheep still cannot vote, even though they outnumber the people.
nsw: The roof of the Sydney Opera House is covered with more than one million tiles. Some people see sails, others see seashells - everyone sees a postcard.
ec: Ecuador is simply the Spanish word for 'equator', which runs just north of its capital, Quito. That is a country name that gets straight to the point.
pe: Peru grows thousands of kinds of potatoes, in colors from yellow to purple. Boring fries are simply not an option there.
ar: Aconcagua in Argentina is 6,961 meters high, the tallest mountain outside Asia. Every other mountain in the Americas, Africa and Europe has to look up to it.
cl: Chile owns Easter Island, where almost 900 giant moai statues look like heads. In fact, many of them have bodies - they are just buried underground.
co: The wax palm, Colombia's national tree, is the tallest palm in the world and can reach up to 60 meters. It is basically a giant feather duster for the clouds.
br: Brazil is named after brazilwood, a tree with red wood that was once shipped to Europe. A whole country named after a tree - talk about deep roots.
eg: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure on Earth for about 3,800 years. That is a very long time at the top of the ranking.
za: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein. Each one hosts a part of the government, so moving offices must be a big project.
ke: Every year more than a million wildebeest, plus zebras and gazelles, migrate between Kenya's Maasai Mara and Tanzania's Serengeti. It is the biggest rush hour in the animal kingdom.
ma: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859, is considered the oldest university still operating in the world. It has been handing out homework for more than 1,100 years.
et: Ethiopia has its own calendar with 13 months, and its year number runs about seven years behind most of the world. So there it is still 'seven years ago' - and New Year comes in September.
ng: Nigeria is the most populous country in Africa, and its film industry, Nollywood, makes more films every year than Hollywood. That is a lot of popcorn.
jm: Reggae was born in Jamaica, and in 2018 UNESCO added it to its list of cultural heritage. The beat is now officially protected.
cu: Because of long limits on imports, many cars in Cuba are from the 1950s, kept running by clever repairs. Some of them are more repair than car.
ca: Canada has the longest coastline in the world, more than 200,000 kilometers. Walking all of it would take a very long time and require very good boots.
us: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France and was shiny brown copper when it was new. It turned green with age - the world's biggest aged penny.
mx: Mexico City is built on top of Tenochtitlan, the old Aztec capital that stood on an island in a lake. The lake was drained, and parts of the city are slowly sinking.
th: Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest city names in the world, so locals just call it Krung Thep. That is a very sensible shortcut.
id: Indonesia is made of more than 17,000 islands. If you visited one island every day, it would take you more than 46 years to see them all.
jp: Mount Fuji is an active volcano, and its last eruption was in 1707. It has been napping for over 300 years, so let's not wake it.
in: The Taj Mahal took about 20 years to build, and it is a tomb that an emperor made for his wife. That is longer than most home renovations.
kr: South Korea has a public holiday just for its alphabet: Hangul Day. King Sejong the Great and his scholars designed Hangul in the 1440s, and it is famous for being easy to learn.
cn: The Great Wall is not one wall but many wall sections built over centuries, adding up to more than 20,000 kilometers. And no, you cannot see it from space with the naked eye.
